content.rendered:
Set your mind on things above, where Christ is. Not on earthly things. The view from above is real. The view from below is partial. The believer is invited to live by the upper view.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, June 17, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Since, then, you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.”
Colossians 3:1-2 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul begins this passage with a fact and ends it with a command. The fact: you have been raised with Christ. The command: now live like it. The verb he uses for set your mind is in the present continuous tense. Keep setting. It is a daily, hourly, moment-by-moment redirection of attention from what is below to what is above.

Things below is not the same as things bad. Paul is not asking the Colossian believers to despise their work, their families, or the ordinary stuff of life. He is asking them to refuse to let those things become the whole horizon. The believer who has been raised with Christ has access to a perspective that earth alone cannot offer. There is a throne. Christ is seated on it. Everything happening below is being seen, weighed and ultimately judged by the One who is seated above.

To set the mind on things above is to look at every below-thing through the lens of above-things. The bill on the kitchen counter is real. The God who supplies all your needs according to His riches in glory is more real. The conflict with a coworker is real. The reconciliation Christ has already accomplished between you and the Father is more real. The grief that has come into the family is real. The promise that God works all things together for good is more real. The earthly things stay. The mind moves above. And from above, the earthly things look smaller than they did when they were the only thing on the screen.

This is not denial. It is altitude. The same mountain that looks insurmountable from the valley looks crossable from the peak. The believer who walks with mind set above is not pretending the valley is not there. They are walking through it carrying the perspective of the peak.

So today, deliberately. Before you check the inbox. Before you scroll the feed. Before you absorb the news. Set your mind above. Where Christ is. Seated. Reigning. And from that throne, everything below has its proper size.

Prayer

Father, today I set my mind on things above. I lift my eyes from the noise of the earthly to the steady reality of the heavenly. Christ is seated at Your right hand. From that throne, every problem on my list has its proper size. Help me to walk through this day carrying the perspective of the peak, not the panic of the valley. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I have been raised with Christ. My mind is set on things above. I see every below-thing through the lens of above-things. The throne where Christ is seated is the perspective from which I walk through this day.
